turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero in the gradebook, and why nobody called me first.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
Walk me through it after you answer my question. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.
I'm writing down 11:31 PM. A file being created at night doesn't tell me who wrote what, Hale. Turn the screen so I can read the history myself.
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
I'm writing down 612 and 794. You said "mostly in one paste," and I want to see where the history says that, not hear it from you. I asked you to turn the screen, Hale.
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
Don't manage me, Hale. The screen, the history page, now.
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.
I'm writing that down. Which three editions, and what act and scene does the essay give for that line? Hand me the page with the quotation on it.
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Then why are we here? I asked which three editions and what act and scene the essay cites, Hale. Answer that.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.
I'm writing down October 15. A student changing his argument between an outline and an essay is called writing, Hale. Is that outline in front of you, or are you telling me what it says?
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.
A machine's guess. Even the company that sells it says not to use it alone, and your own procedure, 4.3, says the same. You didn't answer me about the outline, Hale.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
You're asking me how to do your job? There's no off the record in this room, Hale. Withdraw the zero, and then answer my question about the outline.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.

I've read 4.4, Hale. It follows a concern, and so far you've told me about a concern; you haven't shown me one. The zero comes off today, and if a rewrite is ever on the table I want to know who supervises it and where, because it will not be in front of his class.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? I have a call at 4:40, Hale. The zero, and who supervises the rewrite.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.

Take it to whoever you like, Hale; I'll be in the principal's office when we're done. You entered a zero before calling me, against your own 4.2, and now you're threatening me with a deadline. I'm writing that down.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither. The zero comes off, and then you show me the history page, the outline and the three editions, Hale, in writing.
